The slug-spelling apply's three writes in the page's own transaction: copying fact and take purge tombstones to the moved page's normal name, and re-keying its attachments. Only a page stored under an older spelling reaches them, which the Rust store never holds (it writes every slug in normal form), so they stay raw SQL and are the typed raw_sql refusal there (docs/designs/RUST_ENGINE.md, the slug-spelling apply row).

The preview scan and the per-page re-check read pages, sources and files with SQL like the sibling repairs (legacy-twins, rename-identity), and the collision check looks up every stored spelling of a name through the spelling index (raised from 9: the move counts the attachments updateSlug carries, for its report); a typed method comes with the Rust store serving these members.
